meta.message: Generated project is in workspace/ (cd there and run `python -m pytest`).
limitations: Offline mode: agents use deterministic strategies and domain blueprints (URL shortener, the bundled brownfield sample). Other domains/repositories need `--llm anthropic`.
Generated service uses SQLite and an in-process cache/queue: correct and tested, but not the production stack for the stated scale target (see scaling path).
No authentication/authorization on the API (documented risk).
Load/performance targets are design targets; no load test is executed by the pipeline.
Validation proves the generated tests pass and the contract matches; it cannot prove the tests are exhaustive - human review at G3 remains essential.

spec.raw: We need a links thing that's fast and has some stats. Maybe users too?
spec.title: URL shortener service
spec.intent: Let clients turn long URLs into short codes that redirect, persist them durably, and report how links are used.
functional: Create a short link for a valid http(s) URL via REST API
Redirect GET /{code} to the target URL
Fetch and delete link metadata via REST API
Record clicks and expose per-link analytics
Persist links and analytics durably across restarts
non_functional: Redirect hot path does no synchronous writes (analytics are asynchronous)
Short codes are non-sequential and not enumerable
Horizontally scalable stateless API tier; storage behind a repository interface
Consistent JSON error model; no internal details leaked on errors
Input validation on every external field (URL scheme, length, body size)
Performance: p99 redirect latency < 50 ms (server side) with cache
Scale target: 1k creates/s, 50k redirects/s at peak (design target); 100M links/year
out_of_scope: User accounts / authentication (documented as a follow-up)
Link previews / malware scanning (documented as a risk)

architecture.style: layered service (API -> service -> repository), async analytics pipeline

components.name: API layer (WSGI)
components.responsibility: routing, JSON (de)serialisation, error mapping, request ids, per-client rate limiting

components.name: ShortenerService
components.responsibility: business rules: validation, code allocation with collision retry, redirect resolution

components.name: Repository (SQLite)
components.responsibility: persistence behind a LinkRepository protocol; swappable for PostgreSQL

components.name: Redirect cache
components.responsibility: TTL+LRU cache for the read-heavy redirect path

components.name: Click recorder
components.responsibility: async, batched, load-shedding click ingestion off the hot path

decisions.decision: Random 7-char base62 codes + unique constraint + retry
decisions.rationale: No single coordinator, codes are not guessable, collisions are ~1e-12 per insert at 1M links and handled by retry. Counter needs a sequence service; hashing makes duplicates/collisions deterministic.

decisions.alternatives: synchronous insert per redirect; external queue (Kafka) + stream processor
decisions.rationale: Keeps redirect latency independent of write load. In-process queue is the simplest step; the ClickRecorder interface is where a Kafka/Kinesis producer plugs in at scale.
301 is cached by browsers so later clicks are never counted and links cannot be re-pointed or expired; 302 preserves analytics accuracy at the cost of extra requests.

decisions.decision: Standard-library WSGI + SQLite for the prototype
decisions.rationale: Zero dependencies so reviewers can run it anywhere. Layering (API -> service -> repository protocol) keeps the swap to Postgres/Redis local to two modules.
O(1) total-click reads; detailed roll-ups come from an indexed events table.

scaling_path: Stateless API instances behind a load balancer; scale horizontally.
Move storage to PostgreSQL (primary + read replicas); shard links by hash(code) beyond ~1B rows.
Shared Redis cache in front of the DB for redirects (>95% hit rate expected on popular links).
Replace the in-process click queue with Kafka; aggregate with a stream job into an OLAP store.
CDN/edge redirects for the hottest codes; keep 302 semantics for analytics accuracy.

risks.title: Abuse for phishing/malware redirects
risks.mitigation: Rate limiting on creation is in place; add URL reputation checks (e.g. Safe Browsing) and an abuse report/takedown flow before public launch

risks.title: Open, unauthenticated write/delete API
risks.mitigation: Prototype assumption. Add API keys/OAuth and per-owner authorization before exposure; DELETE must be owner-only.

risks.title: SQLite write contention at the stated scale target
risks.mitigation: Repository protocol isolates storage; migrate to PostgreSQL (+ read replicas, sharding by code hash).

risks.title: Analytics loss on crash or queue overflow
risks.mitigation: Batched flush every 0.5s bounds loss; dropped events are counted and exposed on /healthz; move to Kafka for durable ingestion.

risks.title: Per-instance cache serves stale data after delete
risks.mitigation: TTL bounds staleness; deletes invalidate locally; use shared Redis with pub/sub invalidation when running multiple instances.

risks.title: Hot links overload a single DB row (click_count)
risks.mitigation: Counter updates are batched per flush; at higher scale use sharded counters or stream aggregation.

risks.title: In-process rate limits are per instance
risks.mitigation: Acceptable for prototype; use a shared token bucket (Redis) behind a load balancer.

tradeoffs.gain: accurate analytics, links can expire/be deleted
tradeoffs.cost: every click hits the service (no browser caching)

tradeoffs.gain: redirect latency independent of analytics writes
tradeoffs.cost: stats are eventually consistent (pending_events exposed); small loss window on crash
requires uniqueness check + retry; slightly longer codes than a counter
not the production stack; swap required for the scale target

failure_scenarios.behaviour: API returns 500 with generic error; /healthz reports degraded; analytics flush failures are logged and retried next interval
unique constraint -> retry up to 5 times -> 503 (never overwrites)
served from cache; click queue absorbs bursts, sheds load (counted) when full
400/413 with stable error shape; no stack traces
